story: Djibouti is a country of about a million people that matters far more than its size suggests, because it sits on the Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow strait where the Red Sea meets the Gulf of Aden and much of Europe-Asia trade passes. The US, China, France and Japan all have military bases there, and the rent, along with Ethiopia's port traffic, keeps the economy running. That strategic value has also helped one family keep running the country.

On 10 April, President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, 78, won a sixth term with 97.81 percent against a single challenger, a former ruling-party member (AP via WSLS). He had promised his fifth term would be his last; then, in October 2025, parliament unanimously scrapped the 75-year age limit that stood in his way. The two main opposition parties have boycotted every election since 2016, after he abolished term limits in 2010 (International IDEA). Guelleh succeeded his uncle, Djibouti's first president, in 1999. Foreign powers that depend on their bases there have said little.
briefing.power: A presidential republic in form, a dominant-party state in practice. The president is directly elected for five years with no term limit and appoints the prime minister and government; the ruling coalition dominates the National Assembly.
briefing.holders: President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, in office since 1999.
